title: cost-optimization: autotune batching/caching defaults + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Emily Chen
description:
This PR introduces an end-to-end cost-optimization automation flow: sensible defaults for batching and KV caching, model quantization profile plumbing, and the first version of unit-economics tooling used by the optimizer/autotune pipeline. Motivation: teams repeatedly tune batching/caching/quant settings per workload; automating safe defaults and exposing unit-econ signals enables consistent cost reductions without manual tuning. Changes include runtime defaults, a quantization profile registry, a heuristic-driven autotune controller, and a lightweight unit-econ service that records per-route tokens, latency, and estimated cost delta for profile candidates. Checklist:
- [x] Add batching and KV-cache defaults + feature flags
- [x] Implement quantization profile registry and migration script
- [x] Autotune controller to suggest and evaluate profile changes
- [x] Unit-econ service and console integration (first-pass metrics)
- [x] Backwards-compatible flags and rollout plan
- [x] Tests (unit + integration + canary perf)
- [x] Docs and release notes
See README/CHANGELOG for runtime knobs and console screenshots. This description contains the high-level motivation, rollout plan, and testing notes. Do not rely on this PR alone for production rollout; follow canary steps in the rollout section.
commits: Init autotune controller, basic evaluation loop
Add quantization profile registry and migration script
Runtime: apply batching/caching defaults and feature gating
Console: add unit-econ dashboard and profile suggestions UI

testing_summary: Unit tests added for registry and controller; integration canary run executed against staging 2026-02-20 with 24h traffic replay. Canary measured safe fallback behavior under overloaded nodes. Manual QA: console suggestion flow and accept/revert actions validated.
perf_impact_summary: Canary results (staging, mixed production-like workload): median latency change +1.6ms, p95 change +4ms for long sequences; throughput improved 8% under bursty traffic due to better batching; unit-econ estimates show 18-34% per-token cost reduction for quantizable models (gpt-compat small/med variants), conservative estimate 12% across mixed workloads. Autotune includes rollback thresholds to avoid quality regressions.
release_notes:
- Introduce autotune controller for batching/caching defaults and quantization profile suggestions
- Add quantization profile registry and migration
- Add unit-economics service and console dashboard (preview)
- Feature flags: enable_autotune_quant_profiles, enable_autotune_batching_defaults
Notes: Rollout via canary; on-prem customers must run migration script and may opt-out.
migration_instructions: Run migrations/20260212_add_quant_profiles.sql on control-plane DB; set feature flag enable_autotune_quant_profiles=false if you want to opt out. See docs/releases/2026-02-23-cost-optimization.md for detailed steps.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy to staging and run canary traffic replay for 24h. 2) Gradual rollout to 5% production traffic for 48h, monitor unit-econ metrics and quality evals. 3) Expand to 25% then 100% with automated rollback on quality or latency SLO breaches.
notes: This is the first public iteration of the unit-econ tooling; future work will add model-specific microbenchmarks and tighter integration with dedicated capacity autoscaling policies.
